_comment: Canonical BPM for songs Deezer lacks (bpm:0) OR returns a clear half/double-tempo artifact. Key = 'artist|title'; punctuation/case are normalized at load, so 'AC/DC|...' matches. Deezer's classic-rock BPM coverage is sparse, so the rock canon lives here.

overrides._double_tempo_corrections: below: Deezer reported ~2x the real tempo
overrides._classic_rock_canon: below: Deezer returns bpm:0 for these
overrides._recent_hits_deezer_getsongbpm_lack: too new for the free sources; well-documented tempos
overrides._top100_recognizable_deezer_bpm0: added with the cross-genre top-100 batch; Deezer returns bpm:0 for these, so canonical published tempos live here
overrides._top100_double_tempo_corrections: added with the top-100 batch; Deezer reported ~2x (or 1.5x) the real tempo for these — corrected to the feel tempo
overrides._bpm_audit_2026_07_targets: Flagged as obviously wrong, settled against songbpm.com + tunebat + GetSongBPM. See .dev/reference/gsb-eval.md. Aerials: Deezer had bpm:0 so GetSongBPM's bogus 200 shipped; real driving pulse is 158 (felt 79). Let It Be: Deezer's 138 is a double-time artifact; felt ballad tempo is 72.
overrides._bpm_audit_2026_07_reconcile_guard: The auto-reconcile rule would wrongly halve this to ~80 (clean 2x, fast side >=150) — but the 1966 original is GENUINELY ~160; the 80 is the artifact. Pin it so the rule can't touch it.
overrides._bpm_audit_2026_07_deezer_doubled: Deezer (and the Spotify-lineage DBs) reported ~2x; felt tempo verified as the lower value.
overrides._bpm_audit_2026_07_source_outlier: One machine source misread (not a clean half/double); the databases agree on the value below.
overrides._bpm_audit_2026_07_gsb_halved: GetSongBPM halved a genuinely fast song; felt tempo is the HIGHER value. The auto-rule leaves these alone (fast side <150), so pin them here.
overrides._bpm_audit_2026_07_half_double_felt: Genuine half/double songs — the felt/tapped (slow) octave was chosen for the tempo axis over the faster driving pulse.
